content: The recommended dosing for Cetraria islandica (commonly known as Iceland moss or eryngo-leaved liverwort) is 4 to 6 grams per day, divided into three doses taken orally. Alternatively, 5 to 3 grams of the dried plant can be steeped in 150 mL of boiling water for 5 to 10 minutes, then strained, and consumed as one cup several times daily. This plant is traditionally used for conditions such as bronchitis, cough, fever, dyspepsia, appetite loss, sore throat, and vomiting. It exhibits anti-inflammatory, antiemetic, and demulcent properties and is also reportedly a galactagogue (a substance that promotes lactation). At routine doses, no adverse effects have been reported. However, excessive doses or prolonged use may lead to gastrointestinal irritation and liver problems. In rare cases, external application of the plant may cause sensitivity reactions. Regarding pregnancy and lactation, no adverse effects are known. It is classified as Pregnancy Category A, meaning it is generally considered safe, with controlled studies in pregnant women showing no evidence of fetal risk.
